newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda denies Zairean charges of role in fighting.
newsitem.headline: Uganda denies Zairean charges of role in fighting.

text.p: Uganda on Friday denied Zairean government accusations that it had joined with Rwanda and Burundi in fighting a war in eastern Zaire and called for peace.
"The government would like to stress that there is absolutely no element of truth in this allegation," said a Ugandan government statement quoted by state Ugandan radio.

"Uganda, which has spearheaded efforts to resolve conflicts in the Great Lakes Region by peaceful means, is very sorry and deeply concerned about this accusation," said the government statement, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
"We are unreservedly willing to have observers come to Uganda to verify that we are not at all involved," it added.
It said Uganda had assisted Zaireans who had been displaced by the fighting in eastern Zaire by providing them with safe passage through Ugandan territory to places they considered safe inside Zaire.
"Uganda calls upon all the parties involved in the current conflict in Zaire to desist from any actions that can lead to the further escalation of this conflict," the government added.

Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo told an emergency session of parliament on Thursday: "The government will not undertake any negotiation, will not participate in any regional conference while a part of national territory is occupied by foreign forces."

"This war which the combined forces of Uganda, Burundi and Rwanda are waging against Zaire has brought to broad daylight Rwanda's intention not to welcome on its territory its nationals living in Zaire and to pursue its insane plan of annexing a part of our territory."
State radio said on Friday Zaire's transitional parliament voted to sever diplomatic relations with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda. It was not clear when the move would formally take effect.
Burundi and Zaire have also denied sending troops to fight alongside Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire. But Rwanda has said some of its soldiers entered Zaire earlier this week to stop Zairean firing.
